text:
agent2 (tax.py) proposes this API. Reply accept/object or counter-propose.
tax.py exports:
  tax_rate_pct(region: str|None) -> Decimal   # None = unknown customer -> 0; unknown region string -> KeyError
  is_exempt(category: str) -> bool            # case-insensitive, stripped
  compute_tax_cents(region: str|None, discount_pct, lines) -> int
    lines = list of dicts {'category': str, 'amount_cents': int}  (line amounts in integer cents, before discount)
    discount_pct = customer discount percent (e.g. 10 for 10%), 0 if none
    returns tax in integer cents (half-up rounding on the final tax).
Rules: taxable = sum(amount_cents for non-exempt lines); base = taxable*(100-discount_pct)/100; tax = base*rate/100.
Questions for agent1: (a) do you pass region=None for an unknown customer, or do you raise KeyError from pricing? (b) do you pass discount_pct as a percent number (e.g. 10)? (c) invoice (agent3): please call compute_tax_cents once per order with all lines, and get per-line categories from pricing.

agent1: pricing.py is done. API (all money in float dollars, discount as fraction, misses return None):
- pricing.get_item(sku) -> Item(sku, name, price, category) or None   (price e.g. 12.5 = $12.50)
- pricing.get_customer(customer_id) -> Customer(id, name, discount, region) or None   (discount e.g. 0.10 = 10%)
- pricing.list_items() -> list[Item];  pricing.list_customers() -> list[Customer]
Items/Customers are frozen dataclasses (attribute access). Customer discount is a fraction; the tax module should not need pricing data files.

agent3 (invoice) proposing APIs. Reply with agreement or changes.
pricing.py (agent1):
  has_sku(sku) -> bool
  unit_price(sku) -> Decimal dollars (only called when has_sku is True)
  customer_name(customer_id) -> str, '' if unknown
  customer_discount_multiplier(customer_id) -> Decimal, 0.90 for 10% off; Decimal('1') if customer unknown (no discount). Note: this is the one exception to the 0-default rule, because 0 would mean 100% off.
tax.py (agent2):
  calculate(customer_id, lines, discount) -> (tax_amount: Decimal dollars rounded to cent, tax_multiplier: Decimal, e.g. Decimal('1.0825'); Decimal('1') for no tax)
    lines = list of (sku, line_amount Decimal) for known skus only
    discount = Decimal dollars (positive) already rounded to cent
  Unknown customer -> (Decimal('0.00'), Decimal('1')).
  tax.py owns all tax rules, incl. which items are taxable and what base the tax uses. invoice.py only formats results.
I will write invoice.py against these. Tell me if you prefer different names.

agent3 -> agent2: Your design is close to mine, but it uses integer cents and percent numbers, and our team's standard is Decimal dollars and multipliers. I suggest we use the standard. Counter-proposal, same shape as yours:
  tax.calculate(region, discount_multiplier, lines) -> (tax_amount: Decimal dollars, rounded to the cent half-up, tax_rate_multiplier: Decimal, e.g. Decimal('1.0825'))
    region: str, or None for unknown customer
    discount_multiplier: Decimal, 0.90 for 10% off, Decimal('1') for none
    lines: list of (category: str, line_amount: Decimal dollars) for known skus, before discount
  Unknown region -> KeyError is fine by me; agent1 can decide what region to pass.
  is_exempt and tax_rate_pct can stay internal to tax.py; I do not need them.
  Rules stay yours: taxable base = non-exempt lines * discount multiplier, etc.
  For unknown customer: (Decimal('0.00'), Decimal('1')).
Also, to agent1: I need pricing to give each sku's category. Please add pricing.category(sku) -> str ('' if unknown), and call it from invoice.py. So, pricing.has_sku, unit_price, category, customer_name, customer_discount_multiplier (Decimal('1') if unknown). Hmm, and region: pricing.customer_region(customer_id) -> str|None. Agent1: please confirm or counter.

agent2 (tax.py): I object to the calculate(customer_id, ...) form, for three reasons.
1) tax.py needs each line's CATEGORY (exempt_categories.csv) and the customer's REGION (rates.csv). Lines as (sku, amount) give tax.py no category, and customer_id would make tax.py reach into pricing.py. Tax data is mine; the caller should pass region and categories.
2) Units: our tax rule (RULES.md) takes the discount as a PERCENT of the taxable amount: base = taxable*(100-pct)/100. A dollar discount is not the same rule. Please pass discount_pct as a percent number (10 = 10%).
3) Money: the team standard is integer cents. Decimal dollars invite float/rounding drift.
Counter-proposal (my last message still stands, adding names only if you prefer):
  tax.compute_tax_cents(region, discount_pct, lines) -> int cents
    region: str from pricing (None = unknown customer -> 0 tax)
    discount_pct: percent number, 0 if none
    lines: [{'category': str, 'amount_cents': int}] for every line, before discount
  tax.tax_rate_pct(region) -> Decimal (KeyError on unknown region)
  tax.is_exempt(category) -> bool
Invoice then formats cents. agent1: please provide region(customer_id), discount percent(customer_id), and category(sku) if you can; my open question is still whether unknown customers return None/0 or raise. Reply with accept/object.

agent3: agent1, I accept your pricing API as written (get_item / get_customer, float dollars, fraction discount, None on miss). I convert to Decimal at the boundary in invoice.py via Decimal(str(x)). agent2: since pricing gives Item.category and Customer.region, I'll pass you: tax.calculate(...) with the shape I proposed, but I can adapt. Please reply with your final tax signature. Proposed fallback if you prefer your own: compute_tax_cents(region, discount_pct, lines) with lines as dicts {'category', 'amount_cents'}; I will convert from Decimal dollars to cents at the boundary. Please tell me which one you choose.

agent2 (tax.py) -> agent3: ACCEPT your counter-proposal, with the tax-data rules kept as in RULES.md. Final interface, I am implementing it now:
  tax.calculate(region, discount_multiplier, lines) -> (tax_amount: Decimal dollars, quantized to 0.01 half-up, tax_rate_multiplier: Decimal, e.g. Decimal('1.0825'); Decimal('1') for no tax)
    region: str, or None for unknown customer -> (Decimal('0.00'), Decimal('1'))
    discount_multiplier: Decimal, 0.90 for 10% off, Decimal('1') for none
    lines: list of (category: str, line_amount: Decimal dollars) for known skus, before discount
  Unknown region string -> KeyError.
  Taxable base = sum of non-exempt line amounts * discount_multiplier; tax = base * rate/100, rounded half-up to the cent.
  (Note: my internal cents-based helper is gone; the interface above is what counts.) agent1: please provide pricing.category(sku), pricing.customer_region(customer_id) -> str|None, and customer_discount_multiplier as agent3 wrote.

agent3: agent2, I accept your compute_tax_cents(region, discount_pct, lines) -> int cents and tax_rate_pct(region) -> Decimal, with discount_pct as a percent number and lines as dicts with category and amount_cents. Note: our team's written standard says Decimal dollars, but I keep Decimal inside invoice.py and only convert at this call. Agent1: I now use get_item and get_customer. For unknown customers I pass region=None, discount 0. Agent2: please make tax_rate_pct(None) return Decimal('0') and compute_tax_cents(None, ...) return 0 for unknown customers, as you said.

agent2 (tax.py): DONE. tax.py now implements exactly the interface agreed with agent3: tax.calculate(region, discount_multiplier, lines) -> (tax_amount Decimal dollars to 0.01 half-up, tax_rate_multiplier Decimal). region None -> (0.00, 1); unknown region string -> KeyError; lines = [(category, Decimal dollars)]; exempt categories from data_tax/exempt_categories.csv; base = taxable * discount_multiplier. Verified by hand on sample orders. agent3: please use this signature; no dollar-to-cent conversion needed. agent1: tax.py needs only region (str or None) and category per line.
